title: AUDIOJUNKIE: The Ella Langley effect

blocks.text: By now you’ve probably heard the song “Choosin’ Texas” by Ella Langley on the radio. I don’t know about FM radio in Manila, but in the US, Langley is ridin’ high. I mean, I always hear “Choosin’ Texas” every time I open my radio. More often while driving, in the morning, which I never miss, and once more in the evening on my way home. There’s something to be said about that. For one to play on radio so dominantly (even in this day and age) you’ve got to be a big time artist. And these days, no one is as big as Langley. By now, “Choosin’ Texas” has already spent 45 weeks in the Hot 100 Billboard Charts. I don’t know how long it stayed on number one, but as I’m writing this, it’s still enjoying the top spot as we speak. Now that’s something! Ok, I researched it: “Choosin’ Texas” has spent 20 weeks (!) on the singles charts. Not only that, in its course, it has broken and made several records among which, it is the longest female song on the chart, beating out Mariah Carey and BoyZ II Men’s “One Sweet Day.” It is also the longest leading non-holiday song in the charts’ history. And it is the longest running No. 1 country song by a female artist in the 68-year history of the singles charts. Not bad. But who is Langley, really? Well, she was born May 3, 1999 and she is from Hope Hull, Alabama. This home grown country girl stands about 5’6”. She made her debut as a country artist back in 2024 with a duet (with Riley Green) titled “You Look Like You Love Me.” This song is a ditty, simplistic enough to listen to and sing, and the melody is not that hard to retain, but far from being a hit. But that’s the great thing about artists, you don’t know which of their songs can be a hit. “Choosin’ Texas” is different. After a four-bar intro that can be likened to any classic 80’s country song, the song comes in easy: “Just when I thought I got him to fall in love with Tennessee / I shoulda known better than to take him back to Abilene / I put him right back into her arms / I wasn’t a match for that kinda spark.” I mean, what’s in Abilene? And who is that other woman? From there, you just gotta see where it takes you. You don’t need to be a country music fan (I mean look at me) to be reeled into the mystery. And it’s even plain speak: “She’s from Texas, I can tell by the way / He’s two steppin’ ‘round the room.” Why the hell is he doin’ that? “And judgin’ by the smile that’s written on his face / there’s nothin’ I can do...” Just about seems to seal this sorry girl’s fate! Even the song references are on point! “Smoky Mountain Rain” is a Ronnie Milsap tune, and “them old Hank tunes, the Memphis blues we used to sing” refer to Hank Williams! And “he always loved ‘Amarillo By Morning’” is a George Strait song. That’s an old country gangster roll call right there. But other than that, this brown-haired girl really sings a pretty tune. She’s this season’s Shania Twain; this summer’s Linda Ronstadt; and she’s just about to enter the Dolly Parton era of her career. That’s the Ella-Langley-effect there!
